title: Declared Module semantic policy governs supported operational consequences
statement: Every supported direct or transitive effect attributed to a declared Module MUST satisfy that Module Contract's explicit semantic capability/effect policy; insufficient claim-relative authority MUST remain UNKNOWN.
rationale: Observed operations, derived effects, capabilities, authored permissions, conformance, and enforcement are different facts. Comparing them through one evidence-preserving evaluator makes semantic prohibitions enforceable without inferring permission from implementation.
failure_prevented: Architecturally forbidden filesystem, network, process, environment, time, randomness, panic, unsafe, state, or residual external behavior hidden behind direct or transitive calls.
applicability: Declared Fortress Modules whose canonical Module Contract v3 contains semantic_policy.
evaluation: Fortress consumes the canonical CCG, PSM ownership, State/Effect v2 consequences, and Architecture Realization records. Effect-specific policy overrides capability policy. Unlisted observations remain undeclared. Supported contradictions fail with exact causal evidence; claim-relevant opaque calls produce UNKNOWN rather than PASS.

finding.message: A declared Module exercised a forbidden semantic effect/capability, or an authored prohibition could not be evaluated with required semantic authority.

remediation: Remove the forbidden reachable operation, route it through authorized architecture, improve the unresolved semantic authority, or explicitly revise the Module Contract policy after review. Never infer permission from current behavior.
valid_example: A Module allows filesystem reads, denies filesystem writes, and supported causal evidence contains only std::fs::read.
invalid_example: A Module denies filesystem.write while a supported entry-to-helper call chain reaches std::fs::write.
exception_policy: Only canonical finding-governance baselines or narrow explicit exceptions may change enforcement; raw FAIL or UNKNOWN remains visible.
history: Introduced with explicit Module Contract semantic policy and evidence-preserving effect/capability conformance.
